Class ItemState<T>

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.item.ItemState<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the value's type
public final class ItemState<T> extends Object
A value that rides on an item: "open", "favorite", a mark. It follows the item wherever it goes (into a shulker box and back, dropped, traded), and vanilla syncs it to clients with the stack, so any client drawing the item reads it. The server sets it. 
// Common init:
static final ItemState<Boolean> OPEN = ItemState.flag("mymod:open", ItemState.Saved.NO);

// Server, when the box opens and when it closes:
OPEN.set(ref, true);
OPEN.clear(ref);

// Either side:
boolean open = OPEN.is(stack);

A state is a data component SlotKit registers for the mod. A ItemState.Saved.YES state is saved with the item; a ItemState.Saved.NO state isn't, so it's gone after a relog or a restart. Only a mod declaring bothSides: required declares a state, because a client without the mod can't read the stack. A stack carrying a state doesn't merge with one that doesn't, as with any component: fine for unstackable items and for a flag held briefly. Since 2.2.0.
